correctness.rationale: The uniform integer flex one-cochain α assigning +1 to each sink-to-source directed flex edge is closed: each cubical square has two positive and two negative boundary terms. Kozlov Theorems 5.18 and 6.1 supply the explicitly used non-equivariant deformation retract of every circle component onto an n-edge sink-flip core cycle (and other components contract). Its primitive core generator pairs n with α, so the positive integral generator is unique. Automorphisms preserve sink/source and α, while global reversal J swaps them and sends α to −α; naturality forces the claimed full integral signed permutation action. Rational orbit-space homology equals invariant rational homology for finite cellular group actions after equivariant subdivision, and a signed permutation orbit has a one-dimensional invariant precisely when its stabilizer contains no sign-negative element. The tree corollary uses Kozlov Corollary 6.13. Fresh independent orientation/square enumeration checked path_4 (8 orientations, four squares), cycle_4 (16, two squares), triangle (8, no squares); the general proof depends on the published core theorem, not finite sampling.
residual_risks: Exact n-edge positively traversed core theorem is an explicitly credited primary premise; quotient only rational, since torsion may arise in integer quotients.
